1. Executive Summary  
 
In 2025, SCBX navigated a complex macroeconomic landscape defined by subdued growth and 
heightened uncertainty. While global headwinds and domestic structural vulnerabilities —compounded 
by margin pressure from multiple interest rate cuts —presented signific ant challenges, the Group’s  
strategy remained resilient. SCBX prioritized disciplined cost management and prudent risk control, 
ensuring that SCBX remains positioned to deliver sustainable, long-term value for our stakeholders. 
SCBX delivered a net profit of Baht 47.5 billion in 2025, representing an 8.1% yoy increase despite a 
challenging operating environment. The growth was primarily driven by strong investment gains from 
both the Bank’s and SCB 10X’s portfolios, reflecting effective portfolio management and favorable 
market conditions. Additionally, fee income from wealth management remained robust, driven 
significantly by strategic organizational restructuring and the deployment of AI-powered advisory tools, 
which improved se rvice productivity, alongside favorable market conditions. Conversely, 
bancassurance income softened, primarily reflecting its correlation with our prudent loan consolidation 
strategy. Cost discipline also contributed positively, with a cost-to-income ratio of 40.5%, outperforming 
2025 guidance. These factors partially offset the impact of lower net interest income, which was 
pressured by a declining NIM and negative loan growth. 
Loan volumes declined by 2.1% yoy across both Gen 1 and Gen 2 businesses, reflecting the Company’s 
prudent approach to safeguarding credit quality amid a subdued economic environment. Growth 
remains highly selective, with management prioritizing risk -adjusted returns over volume expansion . 
The Company continues to monitor market dynamics closely and stands ready to recalibrate lending 
strategies as economic indicators stabilize and opportunities emerge. Looking ahead, the Company 
expects gradual recovery in  loan demand and targeted growth initiatives in high -potential segments, 
while maintaining prudent credit discipline. 
Asset quality remained well -managed, with the NPL ratio at 3.29%, compared to 3.37% in 2024, 
supported by enhanced collection efficiency and proactive measures such as the “You Fight, We Help” 
program. New NPL formation remained relatively stable, underscoring the effectiveness of the 
Company’s risk management strategies.  Enhanced collection processes, early warning systems, and 
customer support programs  remain in place to mitigate potential credit deterioration and preserve 
overall asset quality. In line with its prudent provisioning policy, the Company allocated an a dditional 
Baht 4,500 million in Management Overlay (MO) during 2025 to reinforce resilience against potential 
downside risks. As of December 31, 2025, 55% of the total eligible loans under Phase 1 and 2 of 
Measure 1 in the ‘You Fight, We Help’ program had been signed, amounting to Baht 71.6 billion.

2. Thailand’s Economic Outlook  
 
Thailand’s economy in 2025 grew by 2.4%, slowing from 2.9% in the previous year. The deceleration 
reflected weaker private consumption driven by sluggish labor income growth amid a more fragile labor 
market and declining consumer confidence. The tourism sector expanded at a slower pace, with foreign 
tourist arrivals declining to 32.97 million due largely to a sharp contraction in arrivals from China. 
Meanwhile, industrial production continued to contract. Despite these headwinds, the Thai economy 
benefited from solid merchandise export growth, supported by the upturn in the global electronics cycle, 
front-loading of imports by trading partners ahead of higher U.S. tariffs beginning in August and a surge 
in gold exports since the start of the year. Government spending also accelerated after disbursement 
of the annual budget  was expedited. Headline inflation in 2025 registered at -0.1%, marking the first 
contraction in five years, largely attributable to a sharp decline in global energy prices, government cost-
of-living support measures for energy and limited demand-side inflationary pressures. 
In 2026, Thailand’s economic growth is expected to slow further to 1.5% . Downside pressures will be 
driven primarily by external factors, including a slowdown in the global economy resulting from U.S. 
tariff measures and heightened global competition, which together increase the risk of a contraction in 
Thai exports. While the tourism sector is expected to con tinue its gradual recovery, foreign tourist 
arrivals are likely to remain well below 2019 levels amid increasingly intense competition within Asia’s 
tourism market (the so -called “tourism war”). At the same time, structural constraints within the Thai 
economy will tighten. Household debt will remain elevated relative to income, leading to more cautious 
consumption behavior amid ongoing debt deleveraging, while financial institutions maintain a prudent 
stance toward lending to households and vulnerable businesses. Private investment is expected to 
expand only modestly despite support from projects promoted by the Board of Investment (BOI) in high-
potential industries. Spillover effects on the real economy will remain limited due to the rising share of 
imported capital goods in the current phase of  investment. The manufacturing sector will continue to 
recover slowly amid weak demand, declining productivity and heightened competitive pressures from 
abroad, particularly from imported goods, further weighing on Thailand’s overall competitiveness.  
A new government transition may slightly delay the enactment of the FY2027 Budget Act, potentially 
disrupting budget disbursement, particularly public investment, at the start of the fiscal year , which 
begins on October 1, 2026.  Over the medium term, government spending will face tighter fiscal 
constraints amid challenges in fiscal reform aimed at reducing budget deficits and containing public 
debt below the statutory ceiling of 70% of GDP. These will be key priorities for the new  government in 
maintaining confidence among credit rating agencies and safeguarding long -term fiscal stability. 
Headline inflation in 2026 is projected at 0.2%, remaining below the inflation target range due to 
declining global energy prices and weak demand-side pressures. 
In 2025, a series of cuts reduced Thailand’s policy interest rate from 2.25% to 1.25 % and a further cut 
is expected in 2026 to 1.0% to enhance monetary policy accommodation. This stance is consistent with 
Thailand’s economic growth remaining significantly below potential, subdued inflation that has yet to 
return to the target range and the  need to alleviate tight financial conditions, particularly for vulnerable

The Thai baht is expected to weaken from mid-2026 onward, driven by a strengthening U.S. dollar amid

factors may also exert downward pressure on the baht, including Thailand’s low growth outlook and 
elevated political uncertainty. In addition, gold prices are expected to moderate after a strong surge in 
the previous year. By year  end, the exchange rate is projected to range between 32.5 –33.5 baht per

For the fourth quarter and the year ended December 31, 2025 
 
Strategy for 2026  
 
In 2026, SCBX’s strategic focus is to solidify our market leadership in Thailand while strengthening the 
foundations required for our long -term vision of becoming ‘The Most Admired Regional Financial 
Technology Group.’ Against a backdrop of economic volati lity, SCBX is balancing defensive resilience 
with disciplined growth. 
SCBX is embedding AI across our operations to drive structural cost efficiency and operational 
excellence, ensuring our portfolio remains agile and competitive. Simultaneously, the Group  is 
committed to allocating capital and directing resources toward high -quality growth opportunities that 
align with our risk appetite , aiming at long-term value creation to our shareholders.  Underpinning this 
approach is our unwavering commitment to governance and sustainability, ensuring we maintain the 
trust of our stakeholders as we drive the Group’s evolution. 
 
Gen 1 (Banking Business): Strategic Calibration for Sustainable Leadership 
In 2026, SCB Bank is transitioning from  balance sheet optimization to selective growth . Having 
structurally strengthened our asset quality over the past year s, the Bank is now positioned to deploy 
capital into high-quality segments where our scale, brand trust, and funding costs allows us to be in the 
market leading position.  
The Bank  sees a strategic window to re -engage with top -tier corporate clients , w hile we remain 
disciplined on risk. By leveraging our balance sheet strength and offering holistic financial solutions, the 
Bank aims to deepen our position as the main operating bank for leading Thai conglomerates.  
As a market leader in housing loans, the Bank is refining our approach to defend and grow our portfolio. 
The Bank  acknowledges that untapped opportunities exist within the high -credit-quality segment. 
Therefore, the Bank is  enhancing our credit screening capabilities with advanced analytics to identify 
and capture prime borrowers who may have been overlooked by previous, rigid filtering models.  
Wealth Management remains our primary engine for fee income growth, catalyzed by our recent 
strategic organizational restructuring and the deployment of AI -powered advisory tools. These internal 
transformations have structurally uplifted our 'Digital Wealt h with Human Touch' capabilities, enabling 
us to capture value with greater precision independent of market cycles. By leveraging this sharpened 
operating model to maximize share -of-wallet, we are intensifying collaboration across SCBX Group 
companies to drive cross-selling and synergy. 
 
Gen 2 (Consumer & Digital Finance Business): Operational Turnaround & Selective Growth 
In 2026, our Gen 2 businesses are pivoting to a profit turnaround and selective growth. Following a 
rigorous period of strengthening our balance sheet through a disciplined focus on asset quality, CardX

card positioning, and selectively grow ing our personal loan portfolio. With a stronger asset -quality 
foundation and a leaner operating model, CardX is set to competitively expand its market presence, 
supported by AI-driven collections that help ensure credit costs remain well controlled. 
Entering its fourth year of operations, AutoX is transitioning from a phase of rapid network expansion 
to strategic calibration, refining underwriting models and risk parameters to align with current economic 
conditions. Loan g rowth will be deliberate, prioritizing asset quality and portfolio health over sheer 
volume as AutoX optimizes the business model for long -term sustainability. AutoX is also diversifying 
revenue beyond interest income by aggressively expanding insurance fee income  from both lending 
and non-lending customer segments.  
Finally, our pure-play digital lenders, MONIX and ABACUS digital will continue to demonstrate robust, 
high-quality growth. Leveraging proprietary AI engines—such as ABACUS Core Technology (ACT) and 
MONIX’s behavioral scoring—these entities have consistently maintained superior asset quality relative 
to the market. We expect them to remain steady contributors to Group profit, using their data advantage 
to capture underserved segments with precision. 
 
Gen 3 (Platforms & Technology Business): Strategic Capabilities & Cost Efficiency 
Gen 3 companies will continue their strategic mandate in 2026 as the Group’s centralized capability 
engine, tasked with building the critical Data, AI, and Technology infrastructure that powers the entire 
SCBX ecosystem. The primary objective is to drive Group -wide cost efficiency while pre serving the 
optionality to scale when market conditions for new technology, digital assets and platforms become 
more favorable. 
At the core of this strategy, TechX will continue to serve as the Group’s centralized technology 
backbone, driving software development and ensuring that AI are effectively embedded into business 
operations to create measurable value uplift. DataX will continue to serve as the Group’s centralized 
data backbone, strengthening data foundations to ensure that our AI initiatives are supported by high 
quality and trustworthy data. 
Our platform businesses, InnovestX and PointX, serve as the drivers of ecosystem connectivity. By 
deepening collaboration with SCB Bank, particularly in the Wealth segment, they utilize digital 
investment channels and a centralized loyalty infrastructure to enhance customer engagement and 
enable cost-efficient cross-selling. Simultaneously, SCB 10X and Token X anchor our readiness in the 
venture and future finance  space, maintaining a disciplined R&D focus on deep -tech capabilities to 
ensure the Group remains market-ready for future innovation cycles.

2025 Performance and 2026 Action Plans  
 
SCB Bank  
 
In 2025, SCB Bank successfully deepened its AI adoption, embedding artificial intelligence as a core 
driver across product design, service delivery, and risk management. This shift is already bearing fruit: 
by leveraging data to anticipate customer needs, income generated from AI-enabled operations nearly 
tripled compared to those in 2024. Beyond revenue, the Bank strengthened its operational resilience, 
significantly reducing platform downtime and further enhancing system stability. These achievements 
validate our "Digital Bank with Human Touch" st rategy, proving that we can scale AI adoption 
responsibly while delivering the sophisticated advisory services that our clients expect. 
Looking ahead, the Bank will cement its “Digital Bank with Human Touch” strategy by focusing on three 
strategic pillars. First, the Bank will continue to focus on high-quality loan growth, in both the corporate 
and retail segment s, in the areas where we identify opportunity gap s and defend our strong position 
among high-quality customers. Second, the Bank will accelerate fee and investment income  through 
further deepening share -of-wallet in wealth management, increas ing penetration in transactional 
banking, particularly in key products such as cash management, trade finance, a nd foreign exchange, 
and strengthening investment and treasury capabilities by expanding investments within a disciplined 
risk management framework and close risk-monitoring processes. Finally, the Bank will further reinforce 
end-to-end risk management capabilities, maintaining adequate provisions aligned with customer risk 
profiles and accelerating NPL reduction through both internal and external measures. 
 
CardX  
 
In 2025,  CardX successfully executed a strategic turnaround to return to profitability.  This 
recovery was driven by a disciplined focus on asset quality —prioritizing selective growth in lower -risk 
segments—alongside rigorous cost control and a substantial reduction in credit costs through enhanced 
end-to-end risk management.  Structurally, CardX achieved a historic milestone as the first financial 
institution in Southeast Asia to fully migrate its core credit card and personal loan systems to a cloud -
based a rchitecture. This transformation, recognized with The Asian Banker’s  "Best Cloud -Based 
Technology Initiative" award, establishes the scalable data infrastructure required for our next phase of 
AI-driven efficiency. Commercially, our value proposition remains strong, evidenced by the CardX JCB 
PLATINUM winning "Product of the Year," confirming our ability to retain top-of-wallet engagement while 
navigating a recovery year. These achievements position CardX with a clean balance sheet and agile 
infrastructure for sustainable growth in 2026. At the end of 2025, CardX loan outstanding stood at Baht 
86.5 billion. 
Looking ahead to 2026 and beyond, CardX is positioned to be a top-of-mind provider of credit cards 
and personal loans by leveraging data, digital and AI capabilities to further strengthen customer

AutoX 
 
In 2025, heightened macroeconomic uncertainty required prudent risk management. AutoX responded 
by tightening its credit selection criteria to ensure the quality of new loans, resulting in negative loan 
growth. The company fine -tuned its provisioning model  based on three years of operational data. To 
maintain business momentum, the company implemented strict cost controls and pursued non-interest 
income growth through expansion into insurance brokerage services, launching the new platform 
“Chaiyo Care Platform” to support the distribution of non -life insurance. Total loans stood at Baht 47.7 
billion at the end of 2025. 
Looking ahead to 2026, AutoX will focus on strengthening its foundations for sustainable growth. Key 
priorities are high-quality loan selection through advanced customer data analytics and proactive debt 
management in higher risk segments. Concurrently, th e company aims to increase fee -based income 
from insurance brokerage by offering life and non-life insurance products to both lending customers and 
new segments. 
Additionally, AutoX will continue to prioritize operational efficiency by integrating artificial intelligence 
(AI) across all processes — from loan origination to monitoring and day-to-day operations — enhancing 
productivity and driving long-term cost optimization. 
 
MONIX 
 
In 2025, MONIX celebrated its fifth anniversary of empowering Thais to break free from informal debt 
by launching the “Life Fighters” campaign. This initiative honors and supports underserved 
individuals by enabling confident and convenient access to legal credit and reflects MONIX’s long -
standing commitment to financial inclusion over the past five years. This campaign also introduced a 
groundbreaking innovation, “Fastest Approval in 5 Seconds ”. Powered by AI, machine learning, 
alternative data , and biometric verification , this  feature delivers quick, accurate, and secure loan 
approvals - underscoring MONIX’s unwavering commitment to providing an exceptional digital lending 
experience.

InnovestX 
 
Amidst 2025’s volatility, InnovestX achieved strong progress by bridging global investment access with 
superior digital engagement. InnovestX captured surging offshore demand through the strategic launch 
of Depository Receipts (DR) and structured products, rapidly establishing leadership in market 
capitalization and turnover. Concurrently, InnovestX elevated the investor experience by introducing 
precision tools —including portfolio analytics and stock watchlists —and enhancing customer loyalty 
through the integrated InnovestX Point Rewards. Underpinning this ecosystem, InnovestX leveraged 
SCBX Group’s AI capabilities to scale advisory excellence, delivering high -velocity, personalized 
insights across over 1,000 global stocks to ensure precise, data-driven decision-making. 
Looking ahead to 2026, InnovestX is poised for continued growth. InnovestX aims to expand our 
customer base and deliver a good customer experience through a seamless and reliable investment 
platform, enhanced end -to-end sales and services, deeper personalized advisory and 
recommendations, and continual feature upgrades. Through close  collaboration within SCBX Group, 
InnovestX will play a key role in supporting the Group’s broader wealth strategy, delivering integrated 
investment solutions that help unleashing Thais' opportunities to invest. At the same time, InnovestX 
will focus on improving operational efficiency to achieve higher, sustainable profitability.  
 
SCB 10X  
 
In 2025, SCB 10X advanced its three strategic priorities by strengthening its leadership in fintech, 
blockchain & Web3, and AI & deep tech; enhancing technical capabilities and accelerating technology 
transfer; and expanding its regional presence. SCB 10X deepened its AI network through collaborations 
with specialized funds and experts, resulting in 13 AI -related deployments, with about half of direct 
investments co -invested alongside global tier -1 investors. SCB 10X also advanced Thailand’s AI 
ecosystem through innovations such as Typhoon 2, a Thai large language model, and Typhoon Isan, 
the first systematic Isan speech-to-text model, both developed by its R&D team and supported by AWS

As we venture into 2026, SCB 10X remains committed to its moonshot mission to become Southeast

2026 Guidance 
 
In 2026, the Thai economy is  expected to remain under pressure from global trade tensions and 
subdued external demand, while domestic recovery continues at a moderate pace. SCBX projects loan 
growth in the low -to-mid single digit range, reflecting a cautious stance amid economic uncertainties. 
Growth is anticipated to be driven by targeted expansion in the corporate segment, sustained market 
share in the mortgage business at SCB Bank, and incremental contributions from Gen 2 businesses. 
The Net Interest Margin (NIM) is forecast at 3.0 –3.2%, based on the assumption of a single 25 -bps 
policy rate cut during the year. Fee income is expected to grow at a mid -to-high single digit rate, 
supported by strong performance in wealth mana gement, a recovery in bancas surance and 
contributions from Gen 2 businesses. 
The cost-to-income ratio is targeted at low-to-mid 40s, reflecting lower topline income alongside with 
expenses from Vi rtual Bank. Despite these pressures, disciplined cost management remains a key 
priority to maintain operational efficiency. The credit cost is projected at 135 -155 bps, reflecting 
proactive risk management measures and robust collection strategies to mitigate potential asset quality 
challenges in a volatile economic environment.

SCBX Performance in 4Q25 and 2025 (consolidated)  
 
SCBX reported an audited consolidated net profit of Baht 47,488 million for 2025, representing an 8.1% 
increase from Baht 43,943 million in 2024. The improvement was primarily driven by higher investment 
gains, lower expected credit losses, and reduced operating expenses following the divestment of the 
Robinhood business in 2024, along with disciplined cost-control measures. In addition, fee income from 
wealth management continued to expand. These positive factors were partly offset by lower net interest 
income resulting from policy rate cuts and subdued loan growth. 
In the fourth quarter of 2025, SCBX recorded a net profit of Baht 10,144 million, representing a 13.4% 
yoy decline. The decrease was primarily attributable to lower net interest income and higher expected 
credit losses. These factors were partially offset by higher investment gains and lower operating 
expenses, following continued cost discipline and efficiency measures. 
Compared to 3Q25, SCBX’s net profit declined by 15.9% q oq, primarily due to lower net interest 
income and a decrease in investment gains.

In 2025, net interest margin (NIM) declined by 41 basis points y oy to 3.44%, primarily due to lower 
yields across key earning asset categories — loan yields decreased by 41 basis points, interbank 
yields dropped by 40 basis points, and investment yields fell by 30 basis points. These declines 
reflected the impact of f our policy rate cuts in 2025  — implemented in  February 2025, April 2025, 
August 2025, and December 2025, as well as the “You Fight We Help” program. Although funding 
costs also decreased by 15 basis points, in line with the downward trend in market interest rates, the 
reduction was insufficient to off set the sharper decline in asset yields.  
In the fourth quarter of 2025, net interest margin (NIM) declined by 64 basis points y oy and 20 basis 
points qoq, primarily due to lower yields on interbank placements, loans, and investments, as previously 
discussed. This occurred despite a reduction in funding costs, which was insufficient to offset the 
sharper decline in asset yields. For a detailed breakdown of loan yields by segment or product, please 
refer to Additional Financial Information on page 23.
